daniels-1910-08-18.A1:
CRAZY NEGRO SHOT
He Is Killed by Officer Hebert Waites of the Police.
A negro named Daniels, who is said to have gone crazy on religion, was shot and killed today by Officer Hebert Waites of the police. The police was advised that Daniels, armed with a shot-gun, n was terrorizing the people on Howell street. Officer Waites on reaching the scene pacified Daniels and persuaded him to lay down his gun. As the two were going to the station Daniels drew a hatchet from his waist and struck at the officer, who warded off the blow and then fired the fatal shot.

It is only recently that Daniels had been released from jail, where he was held for being crazy. An inquest is to be held this evening.

new-orleans-new-orleans-1910-08-31.A1:
THREE WHITE MEN
ARE CUT BY BLACKS

Row Between Whites and Negroes Re-
sults From Alleged Insult to Pa-
trolman's Wife.
New Orleans, La., Aug. 31.—As the result of insolence displayed by negroes towards a white lady, the wife of Patrolman John Meyers of the police force, three white men and a negro are in the Charity Hospital suffering from knife wounds. The white men claim they were attacked by the blacks, deny they were armed, and cannot account for the injuries of the negro, whom they assert they did not cut. The negro is unconscious.

Tony Grissaffi of No. 1727 Port street is suffering from wounds in the breast and neck; John Schulingkamp of No. 2705 Roman street, has cuts in the right shoulder and arm; William Schulingkamp of the same address was cut in the arms and breast, being slightly wounded. The negro was badly beaten and cut, and at the hospital it is said he may die. The white men state they were not looking for trouble, but only admonished the negroes for their insolence towards Mrs. Meyers.

tom-weaver-seville-1910-08-22.A1:
KILL MAYOR'S ASSAIL ANT.
Georgia Citizens Shoot Negro to Death in the Streets.
CORDELE. Ga., Aug. 22. — Tom Weaver, a negro, was killed to-day in the streets of Seville, a town about ten miles from here, because he attempted to assassinate Mayor Wilson. The negro was fined on Saturday by the Mayor for drunkenness and threatened at the time to get even. This morning the negro went to Mayor Wilson's home, called him out and shot at him but missed. The negro fled but was caught as he raced through the streets and shot to death by citizens.
tom-weaver-seville-1910-08-22.A3:
NEGRO SHOT AT MAYOR IS HANGED BY POSSE
Seville West of Americus Scene of Killing.
(Special to Times-Recorder.)
Cordele, Ga. August 22. News

Cordele, Ga., August 23. News has just reached the city from Seville, a small station on the Seaboard Air Line railway, about twelve miles east of Cordele, of the killing of Tom Weaver, a negro, by a posse of infuriated citizens Monday night about midnight. The trouble grew out of the fact that Weaver, on a drunken spree the night before the killing, had some words with Mayor Wilson, and after resisting arrest he came to Cordele and purchased a shotgun and loaded it with buckshot and returned to Seville, going to Mayor Wilson's residence, calling him out and firing upon him, the load just missing his head, whereupon the negro fled, pursued by Mayor Wilson and a posse of citizens. They chased him to a small house a few miles from Seville, and in their efforts to arrest him, the negro opened fire on the posse. A number of shots were exchanged in which the negro was killed. The members of the posse escaped injury.

Another death was added to the list of fatal boxing bouts in Philadelphia when Frederick Castor, twenty years old, died in a hospital after participating in a six round bout at the Frankd Athletic club with Frank (Spike) Sullivan. Sullivan has been committed to the county prison to await the action of the coroner. Testimony given before a police magistrate tended to show that Castor had the better of the bout, and in the last round while trying to knock out his rival, suddenly fell unconscious. He was rushed to a hospital and despite every effort of physicians they were unable to revive him. The cause of death has not yet been determined.

A counterfeiters' den was discovered in a house at the foot of Lord avenue and First street, Bayonne, N. J., by the police. In addition to a com-

plete outfit of counterfeiters' tools the policemen found that the house was filled with loot from top to bottom. A motorboat believed to have been stolen from Brooklyn was stored in one room and a rowboat in another. Everything was confiscated by the police. Two men and a woman are under arrest.

Tom Weaver, a negro, attempted to assassinate Mayor Wilson of Cordele, Ga. The negro a few days before was fined by the mayor for drunkenness and threatened at the time to get even. He went to Mayor Wilson's home, call d him out and shot at him but missed. The negro fled, but was caught as he raced through the streets and shot to death by citizens.

The Alaska Pacific Steamship company's liner Buckman was held up at sea off the port of Eureka, Cal., by two passengers. Captain Wood was shot and killed by one of the men. The second man was overpowered by the engine room crew. The passenger who shot the captain jumped overboard with a life preserver and escaped.

Packey McFarland, the lightweight, has accepted an offer from Hugh McIntosh, the Australian promoter, to fight four battles in Australia this fall. There Packey will meet Jem Douglas, Jack Nedden, Johnny Summers and Rudy Unholz. All these bouts will be twenty round affairs, and enough time will elapse between them to allow McFarland to be in good condition. After the Australian engagement McFarland will go to England, where McIntosh has promised him another match with Freddie Welch.

The sculling match for the championship of the world between Richard Arnst of New Zealand and Ernest Barry of London was won by Arnst, the champion, by two lengths. The race was rowed upon the Zambezi river in Rhodesia, Africa, a short distance from the famous Victoria falls, over a course of three and a half miles. The stakes were $2,500 a side.

It has become known in Cincinnati that Tex Rickard is back of a plan to take two all American baseball teams on a tour of this country just as soon as the regular season is ended. A team composed of National league star players will play against one composed of American league men, and it is said that they will go to the ten largest cities in this country.

A sculling match for the world's championship is pending between Champion Arnst and Eddie Durnan. Arnst will pass through Canada on his way to England, where he has another race scheduled with Barry on the Thames. Negotiations are under way to get Arnst to stop at Toronto and meet Durnan.
